title: Derived Hom from a finite locally free sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $P$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module, meaning it is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus d}$ on an open cover for finite ranks $d$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $L$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module viewed in degree zero [def-pc-derived-category]. Then the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is represented by the sheaf $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] in degree zero; equivalently, the sheaves $\mathcal E xt^i_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ vanish for every $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (R Hom(K,M) = M tensor^L K^vee for K perfect; a finite locally free module is perfect)

proof.text: The functor $T=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,-)$ on $\mathcal O_Y$-modules is exact. Indeed, on each open $V_a$ of the cover with $P|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$, the definition of sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] (Hom out of a finite direct sum) gives $P^{\vee}|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$ for $P^{\vee}=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,\mathcal O_Y)$, so $P^{\vee}$ is finite locally free in the open-cover sense and $P^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}-$ preserves short exact sequences by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. By [lem-sc-ext-evaluation], evaluation is an isomorphism $P^{\vee}\otimes-\cong T$ natural in the module, so $T$ preserves short exact sequences as well.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (special case K = P[0]); route of the reviewer audit via lem-sc-ext-evaluation and lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact

proof.text: By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ is the Hom complex $\mathcal H om^\bullet(P,\mathcal I^\bullet)$, where $P$ sits in degree zero and $L\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution. Since $P$ is concentrated in degree zero with zero differential, the product formula there reduces to the complex $T(\mathcal I^\bullet)$: terms $\mathcal H om(P,\mathcal I^n)$, differential $T(d_{\mathcal I})$. An exact additive functor preserves kernels and images, hence commutes with cohomology of complexes: $\mathcal H^n(T(\mathcal I^\bullet))\cong T(\mathcal H^n(\mathcal I^\bullet))$ by step 1. As $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to $L$ in degree zero, this is $\mathcal H om(P,L)$ for $n=0$ and $0$ for $n\neq0$; in particular $\mathcal E xt^i(P,L)=0$ for $i>0$. A complex $C$ with cohomology only in degree zero is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] to $\mathcal H^0(C)$ in degree zero, through the quasi-isomorphisms $C\leftarrow(\cdots\to C^{-1}\to\ker d^0\to0)\to\mathcal H^0(C)$. So $R\mathcal H om(P,L)$ is represented by $\mathcal H om(P,L)$ in degree zero.
